one_liner: JavaScript 2D R-tree for rectangles and points with bulk loading; beats the older imbcmdth RTree JavaScript library.
what_it_does: An in-memory, mutable spatial index for 2D bounding boxes in JavaScript (browser or Node.js). You insert your own objects carrying minX/minY/maxX/maxY (or subclass and override toBBox, compareMinX and compareMinY), then call search(bbox) for all intersecting items, collides(bbox) for a yes/no answer, all(), insert/remove/clear, load() for bulk insertion, and toJSON()/fromJSON() to ship a built tree between server and client. It has its own API; no compatibility layer with other R-tree libraries is documented, and k-nearest-neighbour queries live in a separate package (rbush-knn).
how_it_is_fast: Single inserts use a non-recursive R-tree insertion with the R*-tree split heuristics only (split axis by minimum total margin, split index by minimum overlap then area), skipping R*-tree forced reinsertion, which the author found too slow in JS. Bulk loading is OMT (Overlap Minimizing Top-down) packing: items are partitioned into roughly square tiles with a multi-select built on Floyd-Rivest quickselect, filling nodes to target height; bulk insertion into a non-empty tree uses Small-Tree-Large-Tree (the new batch is built as a subtree and grafted in). Search is iterative with an explicit stack and copies a whole subtree without per-item tests when the query box contains a node's box; deletion uses free-at-empty (no reinsertion on underflow).
when_to_use: JavaScript/TypeScript maps, data visualisation, canvas or game code that needs bounding-box queries over 2D rectangles that are inserted and removed over time.
Batch indexing of roughly 10^4 to 10^6 rectangles with load() (README: bulk insertion ~2-3x faster than one-by-one, and queries ~20-30% faster afterwards).
Building an index on a Node.js server and sending it to browsers via toJSON()/fromJSON() with the same maxEntries.
Incremental bulk updates where each batch is spatially clustered (STLT grafting works well for clustered data per the README).
when_not_to_use: Static point sets: the README itself points to kdbush, which indexes points 5-8x faster than RBush.
C or C++ projects: this is a JavaScript library and its benchmark is JS versus JS; use a native sibling instead.
3D or higher-dimensional data, or nearest-neighbour queries without the extra rbush-knn package (RBush is 2D bounding-box search only).
Bulk-inserting scattered data into an existing tree: the README warns this makes query performance worse.
Rapidly moving objects: there is no update operation, only remove plus insert (issue #28, open since 2015); and CommonJS-only environments, since v4+ is ESM only.

integration.form: module (npm ES module; also a UMD browser bundle rbush.min.js exposing a global RBush)
integration.min_toolchain: An ES-module JavaScript environment (RBush v4+ dropped CommonJS); IE11 needs transpiling per the README
integration.thread_safety: not documented (plain single-threaded JavaScript object graph; no locking)

gotchas: remove() matches by object reference by default; with a custom equals function the item you pass must still carry the original bounding box, because the traversal only descends into nodes whose box contains the item's box (index.js remove(); open issue #95).
fromJSON() trusts its input and requires the same maxEntries as the exporting tree; the README's import example still uses the old rbush(9) factory call, while v4 is a class (new RBush(9)).
maxEntries is clamped to at least 4 and minimum fill is 40%; higher maxEntries speeds insertion and slows search (README default 9, benchmark used 16).
search() allocates and returns a fresh array per call, and load() copies the input array (data.slice()) before partitioning it.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among catalogued siblings, pick RBush over KDBush only when you index rectangles or need insert/remove (KDBush is static points and, per RBush's own README, 5-8x faster at that); the native siblings (tidwall/rtree.c, PH-tree, GeoToolbox KdBoxTree) and the Rust geo-index are the choice outside JavaScript.
verified_claims_summary: The README table is a first-party run on Node.js v6.2.2 on a mid-2012 Retina MacBook Pro (CPU model not given) with 1M random rectangles of ~0.01% area and maxEntries 16: one-by-one insert 3.18 s vs 7.83 s for imbcmdth's old RTree, 1000 searches at 0.01%/1%/10% area 0.03/0.35/2.18 s vs 0.93/2.27/9.53 s, removing 1000 items 0.02 s vs 1.18 s (about 59x, derived from page data, printed as 50x), and bulk insert of 1M items 1.25 s (the printed 6.7x does not follow from the table; 7.83/1.25 is about 6.3x, derived from page data). The script the README cites (debug/perf.js) is now bench/perf.js and times RBush alone, so the baseline column cannot be reproduced from the repo.
status_note: Maintained (last commit 2026-04-03, a dev-dependency update; last functional release v4.0.1 per package.json), MIT-licensed, a single ~500-line source file with one dependency, so easy to vendor; 8 open issues, all enhancements or questions.
